'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[Awa Odori]]) held annually during the [[Bon Festival]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==
* {{ill|Kochi Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kochi Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yosakoi Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosakoi Festival|qq=}} – One of the Three Great Festivals of Shikoku. * {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumamoto Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yamaga Lantern Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaga Lantern Festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] ** {{ill|Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|qq=}}
* {{ill|Sabantuy|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sabantuy|qq=}} – A summer festival held along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Volga River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Volga River|qq=}} in {{ill|Russia|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russia|qq=}}.
* {{ill|Haru Matsuri|lt=Haru Matsuri|lt=Spring Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Aki Matsuri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Winter Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Winter Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Tanabata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}} * {{ill|Community building|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Community building|qq=}} * {{ill|Homecoming|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homecoming|qq=}} * {{ill|Summer Vacation|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Summer Vacation|qq=}}

{{Infobox_holiday |Event Name=Tokushima City Awa Odori |English Name= |Type=Regional|Regional |image=Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima.jpg |image Size=300px |image Caption=Tokushima City's Awa Odori |Common Name= |Former Name= |Time of Year=Annually from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] for four days |First Held= |Venue=City area south of [[Tokushima Station]] |Organizer=Awa Odori Future Connection Executive Committee (Established April 8, 2022)<ref name="asahi20220412"/> |Co-organizer= |Sponsor= |Supporter= |Producer= |Number of Exhibitors= |Attendance=Approx. 1,080,000 (in [[2018]])<ref>[https://www.pref.tokushima.lg.jp/file/attachment/483220.pdf Report on Attendance During Awa Odori Period] Tokushima Prefecture Website, August 23, 2018</ref> |Access Name= |Nearest Station=[[JR Shikoku|JR Shikoku]] [[Tokushima Station]] |Direct Bus= |Parking=Three free parking areas (approx. 2,700 spaces), temporary paid parking (approx. 1,700 spaces), city public paid parking (approx. 2,000 spaces) |Website=https://www.awaodorimirai.com/ |Special Notes= }}
'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Dance Festival]]) held annually during the [[:en:Obon|Obon]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==
* {{ill|Kochi Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kochi Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yosakoi Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosakoi Festival|qq=}} – One of the Three Great Festivals of Shikoku. * {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumamoto Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yamaga Lantern Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaga Lantern Festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] ** {{ill|Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|qq=}}
* {{ill|Sabantuy|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sabantuy|qq=}} – A summer festival held along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Volga River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Volga River|qq=}} in {{ill|Russia|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russia|qq=}}.
* {{ill|Haru Matsuri|lt=Haru Matsuri|lt=Spring Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Aki Matsuri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Winter Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Winter Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Tanabata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}} * {{ill|Community building|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Community building|qq=}} * {{ill|Homecoming|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homecoming|qq=}} * {{ill|Summer Vacation|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Summer Vacation|qq=}}

Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==

{{Infobox_holiday |Event Name=Tokushima City Awa Odori |English Name= |Type=Regional|Regional |image=Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima.jpg |image Size=300px |image Caption=Tokushima City's Awa Odori |Common Name= |Former Name= |Time of Year=Annually from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] for four days |First Held= |Venue=City area south of [[Tokushima Station]] |Organizer=Awa Odori Future Connection Executive Committee (Established April 8, 2022)<ref name="asahi20220412"/> |Co-organizer= |Sponsor= |Supporter= |Producer= |Number of Exhibitors= |Attendance=Approx. 1,080,000 (in [[2018]])<ref>[https://www.pref.tokushima.lg.jp/file/attachment/483220.pdf Report on Attendance During Awa Odori Period] Tokushima Prefecture Website, August 23, 2018</ref> |Access Name= |Nearest Station=[[JR Shikoku|JR Shikoku]] [[Tokushima Station]] |Direct Bus= |Parking=Three free parking areas (approx. 2,700 spaces), temporary paid parking (approx. 1,700 spaces), city public paid parking (approx. 2,000 spaces) |Website=https://www.awaodorimirai.com/ |Special Notes= }}
'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Dance Festival]]) held annually during the [[:en:Obon|Obon]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==
* {{ill|Kochi Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kochi Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yosakoi Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosakoi Festival|qq=}} – One of the Three Great Festivals of Shikoku. * {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumamoto Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yamaga Lantern Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaga Lantern Festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] ** {{ill|Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|qq=}}
* {{ill|Sabantuy|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sabantuy|qq=}} – A summer festival held along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Volga River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Volga River|qq=}} in {{ill|Russia|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russia|qq=}}.
* {{ill|Haru Matsuri|lt=Haru Matsuri|lt=Spring Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Aki Matsuri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Winter Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Winter Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Tanabata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}} * {{ill|Community building|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Community building|qq=}} * {{ill|Homecoming|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homecoming|qq=}} * {{ill|Summer Vacation|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Summer Vacation|qq=}}

On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==

'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Dance Festival]]) held annually during the [[:en:Obon|Obon]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==

'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Dance Festival]]) held annually during the [[:en:Obon|Obon]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==
* {{ill|Kochi Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kochi Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yosakoi Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosakoi Festival|qq=}} – One of the Three Great Festivals of Shikoku. * {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumamoto Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yamaga Lantern Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaga Lantern Festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] ** {{ill|Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|qq=}}
* {{ill|Sabantuy|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sabantuy|qq=}} – A summer festival held along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Volga River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Volga River|qq=}} in {{ill|Russia|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russia|qq=}}.
* {{ill|Haru Matsuri|lt=Haru Matsuri|lt=Spring Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Aki Matsuri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Winter Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Winter Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Tanabata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}} * {{ill|Community building|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Community building|qq=}} * {{ill|Homecoming|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homecoming|qq=}} * {{ill|Summer Vacation|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Summer Vacation|qq=}}

{{Infobox_holiday |Event Name=Tokushima City Awa Odori |English Name= |Type=Regional|Regional |image=Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima.jpg |image Size=300px |image Caption=Tokushima City's Awa Odori |Common Name= |Former Name= |Time of Year=Annually from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] for four days |First Held= |Venue=City area south of [[Tokushima Station]] |Organizer=Awa Odori Future Connection Executive Committee (Established April 8, 2022)<ref name="asahi20220412"/> |Co-organizer= |Sponsor= |Supporter= |Producer= |Number of Exhibitors= |Attendance=Approx. 1,080,000 (in [[2018]])<ref>[https://www.pref.tokushima.lg.jp/file/attachment/483220.pdf Report on Attendance During Awa Odori Period] Tokushima Prefecture Website, August 23, 2018</ref> |Access Name= |Nearest Station=[[JR Shikoku|JR Shikoku]] [[Tokushima Station]] |Direct Bus= |Parking=Three free parking areas (approx. 2,700 spaces), temporary paid parking (approx. 1,700 spaces), city public paid parking (approx. 2,000 spaces) |Website=https://www.awaodorimirai.com/ |Special Notes= }}
'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Dance Festival]]) held annually during the [[:en:Obon|Obon]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==
* {{ill|Kochi Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kochi Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yosakoi Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosakoi Festival|qq=}} – One of the Three Great Festivals of Shikoku. * {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumamoto Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yamaga Lantern Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaga Lantern Festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] ** {{ill|Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|qq=}}
* {{ill|Sabantuy|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sabantuy|qq=}} – A summer festival held along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Volga River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Volga River|qq=}} in {{ill|Russia|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russia|qq=}}.
* {{ill|Haru Matsuri|lt=Haru Matsuri|lt=Spring Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Aki Matsuri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Winter Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Winter Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Tanabata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}} * {{ill|Community building|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Community building|qq=}} * {{ill|Homecoming|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homecoming|qq=}} * {{ill|Summer Vacation|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Summer Vacation|qq=}}
*

Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11489823]] Wikidata name: Tokushima Awa Odori Festival [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:59, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox_holiday |Event Name=Tokushima City Awa Odori |English Name= |Type=Regional|Regional |image=Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima.jpg |image Size=300px |image Caption=Tokushima City's Awa Odori |Common Name= |Former Name= |Time of Year=Annually from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] for four days |First Held= |Venue=City area south of [[Tokushima Station]] |Organizer=Awa Odori Future Connection Executive Committee (Established April 8, 2022)<ref name="asahi20220412"/> |Co-organizer= |Sponsor= |Supporter= |Producer= |Number of Exhibitors= |Attendance=Approx. 1,080,000 (in [[2018]])<ref>[https://www.pref.tokushima.lg.jp/file/attachment/483220.pdf Report on Attendance During Awa Odori Period] Tokushima Prefecture Website, August 23, 2018</ref> |Access Name= |Nearest Station=[[JR Shikoku|JR Shikoku]] [[Tokushima Station]] |Direct Bus= |Parking=Three free parking areas (approx. 2,700 spaces), temporary paid parking (approx. 1,700 spaces), city public paid parking (approx. 2,000 spaces) |Website=https://www.awaodorimirai.com/ |Special Notes= }}
'''Tokushima City Awa Odori''' (とくしまし あわおどり) is a [[:en:Obon|bon odori]] ([[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Dance Festival]]) held annually during the [[:en:Obon|Obon]] period from [[:en:August 12|August 12]] to [[:en:August 15|August 15]] in [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]]. It is one of Japan's traditional performing arts, with a history of over 400 years dating back to the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]].
== Overview == [[File:view of Awa Dance from Tokushima-Sogo.jpg|thumb|180px|View of Awa Odori from {{ill|Tokushima Sogo|ja|徳島そごう|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Sogo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to そごう徳島店}}]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 03.jpg|thumb|180px|Women's dance characterized by elegance]] [[File:Awa-odori 2008 Tokushima 07.jpg|thumb|180px|Men's dance using fans]]
In [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], the birthplace of [[:en:Awa Dance Festival|Awa Odori]], the dance festival is held in various locations throughout August. Among them, {{ill|Tokushima City Awa Odori|ja|徳島市阿波おどり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Awa Odori|qq=}} stands out as the largest and most well-known. Each year, the festival attracts between 200,000 and 1.2 million visitors from across Japan to [[:en:Tokushima_(city)|Tokushima City]], which has a population of approximately 250,000.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date=2018-03-22 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/212317 |title=Why Tokushima’s Awa Odori Became an "Event Hell" |publisher=Toyo Keizai Online |accessdate=2020-04-22}}</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|There is a range in estimated total attendance, which is discussed in [[#Discrepancy in Attendance Estimates]].}} Many travel agencies also organize tours for spectators.
The festival begins at 6:00 PM. The area south of [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]] transforms into a {{ill|pedestrian zone|ja|歩行者天国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pedestrian zone|qq=}} from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, immersing the city entirely in Awa Odori. During the daytime, performances are held in city halls (detailed below), and in the early evening, rehearsals can be observed in parks. On the final night, even after the performances at the designated venues have concluded, small spontaneous dance circles continue, with the sounds of gongs and drums echoing throughout the night.
For many years, the festival was co-managed by the {{ill|Tokushima City Tourism Association|ja|徳島市観光協会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Tourism Association|qq=}} and {{ill|Tokushima Shimbun|ja|徳島新聞社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Shimbun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島新聞}}.<ref name="shigikai20170911">Tokushima City Council Meeting Records, September 11, 2017.</ref> However, since 2018, the organizing body has changed annually.
On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
Naming rights have been introduced for some performance venues.<ref>[https://www.awaodorimirai.com/partner Naming Rights Partners] – Awa Odori Future-Preservation Executive Committee. Retrieved August 14, 2024.</ref> == See Also ==
* {{ill|Kochi Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kochi Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yosakoi Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosakoi Festival|qq=}} – One of the Three Great Festivals of Shikoku. * {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumamoto Prefecture|qq=}} ** {{ill|Yamaga Lantern Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaga Lantern Festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] ** {{ill|Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakonojo Rokugatsudo Okage Festival|qq=}}
* {{ill|Sabantuy|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sabantuy|qq=}} – A summer festival held along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Volga River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Volga River|qq=}} in {{ill|Russia|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russia|qq=}}.
* {{ill|Haru Matsuri|lt=Haru Matsuri|lt=Spring Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Aki Matsuri|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Fuyu Matsuri|lt=Winter Festivals|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Winter Festivals|qq=}} * {{ill|Tanabata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}} * {{ill|Community building|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Community building|qq=}} * {{ill|Homecoming|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homecoming|qq=}} * {{ill|Summer Vacation|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Summer Vacation|qq=}}

On March 29, 2018, the Tokushima City Tourism Association was declared bankrupt.<ref name="tsr-net20180330">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.tsr-net.co.jp/news/tsr/20180330_01.html | title=Tokushima City Tourism Association – Former Administrator of Awa Odori | publisher=Tokyo Shoko Research |date=2018-03-30 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> Subsequently, on April 26, 2018, the structure of the "Awa Odori Executive Committee" was reformed, with Tokushima City joining as a member.<ref name="tokushima-city-1"/> That year, the "So Odori" performance was canceled (see below).
In 2019, the festival was operated by the {{ill|Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|ja|キョードー東京共同事業体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyodo Tokyo Joint Venture|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, commissioned by the city. This marked the first time in the festival’s 400-year history that a private company managed the event (as reported by the Nikkei).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO48488260S9A810C1000000/ | title=Tokushima’s Awa Odori Begins – So Odori Revived, First Private Management | newspaper=Nikkei | date=2019-08-12 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref> However, due to {{ill|Typhoon Krosa|ja|令和元年台風第10号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Krosa|qq=}}, performances on August 14 and 15 were canceled.<ref name="asahi20190814">{{Cite news |title=Tokushima City’s Awa Odori Canceled for the First Time in 16 Years Due to Typhoon Krosa |newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital |date=2019-08-14 |url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASM8G2TY1M8GPUTB006.html |accessdate=2019-08-17}}</ref>
In 2020, the festival was entirely canceled due to the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|ja|日本における2019th year コロナウイルス感染症の流行状況|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="tokushima20200421"/> Instead, on November 21 and 22 of that year, a trial event was conducted at [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]], organized by Tokushima City, to assess COVID-19 safety measures.<ref name="asahi20210122">{{Cite news |author=Minoru Ito |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP1P73MXNDTPTLC007.html | title=Awa Odori Trial Event Reveals Challenges in Managing Audience Exits – Tokushima | newspaper=Asahi Shimbun | date=2021-01-22 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2021, the event was significantly scaled down under the theme "2021 Awa Odori – New Normal Model," organized by Tokushima City. The grand finale was held without an audience.<ref name="tokushima20210910">{{Cite news |url=https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/588838 | title=Breakdown of Awa Odori Project Costs Questioned in Tokushima City Council | newspaper=Tokushima Shimbun | date=2021-09-10 | accessdate=2022-04-13 }}</ref>
In 2022, the festival returned to its usual schedule, organized by the newly established "Awa Odori Mirai e Tsunagu Executive Committee" (Awa Odori Future-Preservation Committee).<ref name="tokushima202208182100"/>
The 2023 Awa Odori did not include the paid performance venue at {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}}. A premium box seating area, priced at approximately ¥200,000 per person, was introduced. On August 14, outdoor performances proceeded despite rain due to the approach of {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2023)|ja|台風7号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Typhoon Lan (2023)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 台風第7号}}, but all performances on the 15th were canceled.<ref>[https://www.topics.or.jp/articles/-/941706 【Video】2023 Awa Odori – Tokushima City’s August 15th Performances Canceled] - Tokushima Shimbun Digital, August 15, 2023</ref>
As of 2024, the paid performance venues include [[:en:Aibahama Park|Aibahama Park]] Enbujo, {{ill|Minami-Uchimachi|ja|南内町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minami-Uchimachi|qq=}} Enbujo, and {{ill|Konyamachi|ja|紺屋町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konyamachi|qq=}} Enbujo. Free performance venues include {{ill|Ryogoku-Honmachi|ja|両国本町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryogoku-Honmachi|qq=}} Enbujo and {{ill|Shinmachi Bridge Street|ja|新町橋通り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmachi Bridge Street|qq=}} Enbujo.
